title_masked: Caveat Emptor...Don't always believe the "glowing" reviews
text_masked:
I was compelled to write this review, not only because this is THE worst RRI I have ever stayed at, but because of all the glowing reviews about this place. I am sorry, but these glowing reviews can't possibly be real. I am writing this review on 2/17/12 while sitting in room 307.
This RRI is VERY old and rundown. The popcorn ceiling says it all. The carpet is stained throughout the place and the rooms smell of mold and dampness (I changed rooms since the first room, #115, smelled musty and damp). Lucky me, #307 was no better.
I am a RediCard member and stay at RRI's whenever I can (see my previous review(s) about other RRI's) and I am just amazed at the reviews here. Someone should look into this. If I was RRI, I would come by and take a look for myself. I know I wouldn't want my name on a place like this.
The young man at the counter was friendly and helpful and the lobby looked and smelled good, but the rest of the place, well, Caveat Emptor!

Well, on the plus side, the hotel was only 3-4 blocks from the philadelphia museum, and on the down side, slightly dingy, dark with rude check in guy. The price was better directly on the best western site than on travel sites. Good enough place to stay while in philly if you're main aim is to see the museum. Free parking was a definite bonus, and the rest of the staff were sweet as pie in the city of brotherly love.

The Four Seasons is all about service. Our recent stay was no exception. The location is perfect and puts you in the middle of things. The Bart station is convenient to the hotel and makes the entire city accessible. The rooms are very comfortable and have all the amenities. I would highly recommend this hotel.

Genuine welcome, excellent Gatti's pizza delivery recommendation, near a local #350 bus stop, free shuttle between airport and hotel, big well-placed TV on wall, big full breakfasts. A great Microtel - not your usual Mictrotel.

title_masked: Looked nice but the wrong crowd for a family place
text_masked:
Nicely redone and clean hotel but that is the extent of the positive comments 
Young family for an early flight Sunday morning and found out the quiet time started at midnight. Rowdy drunk 20-30 year old crowd having a good time but at others expense, not a good idea for an airpot hotel .
Had a large room at the back of the hotel ground floor by the main a/c unit and could not sleep all night as I could hear it start up through the single pane windows about every 20 minutes
Seemed like there was a gang element at the hotel (ie clean shaven , muscle bound tatoo'd young men driving tinted out sports car in and out of the hotel all night) Police showed up at about midnight on force to deal with some problem.

I think Kings Inn Motel would be a more appropriate name, but semantics aside, the room was fine. However, I had a bit of trouble finding open electrical outlets to charge my phone and plug in my laptop. I made sure to ask for the WiFi password at the front desk, and had no trouble logging in and using the internet. 
However, the A/C in my room wasn't working! To be fair, I checked in around midnight, so I didn't call for maintenance. To my surprise, the room got quite cold through the night (the thermostat said 63 degrees), and the blankets weren't very thick. Suffice to say, I didn't sleep very well. When I mentioned it to the front desk the next morning, they said they weren't aware of A/C issues in the past, but that they'd take a look at it. Perhaps it was a one-time fluke, but either way, it was a rather poor way to prepare for my interview that day.

good location, great value for downtown phoenix. The owners are friendly and accomodating. the rooms were very clean and very recently renovated. the beds were very comfortable. Only here for a one night stopover. advertised complimentary transport to hotel. assumed could call the courtesy shuttle from airport hotel directory but they are not listed. called the hotel and they said a 24hr advance booking for courtesy transportation was required so we had to take a cab ($22o/w). however they did accomodate the rtn transportation for the next morning on short notice. would definately stay there again.

This is a great location just minutes away from the piers and cable cars, but it was over priced for what it was. Parking was $40 per day in addition to the room rate and breakfast was also extra. The staff were friendly enough and the rooms clean and what you would expect from Holiday Inn, but our room was not ready when we arrived and the consierge was amost just plain rude. A pleasant enough hotel in a great location, but not sure if we would stay again because of the price.

We picked this hotel since we had tickets to three games at Fenway. Our last experience in Boston was that it can be difficult to get a cab back to the main hotel area. This location was perfect - a six minute walk to the game. You can see Fenway from some of the hotel windows. 
Hotel is top notch - lovely rooms, great service. Very clean, all the amenities. 
My only negative comment is that room service (provided by Eastern Standard - a very good restaurant in the hotel) and the menu is a bit limited after 11 pm. We also liked the oyster bar restaurant. 
Overall a very good stay although I'm not quite sure why it's the top rated hotel in Boston - if we weren't going to baseball, we would have thought it was a bit out of the way! However, it is only a five or ten minute walk to Newbury Street. 
We would stay again - especially if we were going to multiple baseball games.

title_masked: Would've been "alright", check out made it "forget it".
text_masked:
Booked well ahead, and requested a room away from the highway, but were assigned on the highway side anyway. Alright, no big deal - yes, you can hear it, but after a few days travelling it wasn't a huge deal... light sleepers, however, should insist on being on the opposite side as the noise is certainly there.
The room was furnished decently and clean, exactly as one would expect but nothing exceptional. A bit dark in the furnishings, but cozy nonetheless. No love lost on the sliding washroom door - no lock and a little gap would be uncomfortable for many no doubt, even we found it a little off-putting (and we're not the shy type). Though the purpose is obviously to cut down on the intrusion of a swing door into the space, the execution left something to be desired. We weren't offered a selection of beds either, and were given a room with two twin beds. For a couple, it made for an uncomfortably cramped night, not to mention the obviously older spring mattresses had lost some resilience over the years - sitting on the edge landed me promptly on the floor at one point as the mattress edge crumpled away beneath me. Good for a laugh, if nothing else, but not the high standard that it seems the property is going for.
Staff were great from check in to room service, always helpful, polite and courteous. Some exception was taken to the valet/bellman whom seemed to disappear each time we started to approach, but could be chalked up to poor timing. The spoiler for the whole stay, however, was on check out. We intended to check our baggage and grab lunch at Pike Market (the hill is very steep - consider heading down 6th to Pike for an easier trek), and checked out at the desk well before noon when no one else was around. As we checked out, the desk agent, Sarah, was efficient if curt in processing us, however she did answer the phone in the middle of our interaction without so much as an "excuse me" and generally appeared disinterested or unhappy. We felt as though we'd interrupted her and were rather unwelcome. Chalking it up to maybe a slight misstep or peculiar moment, we were disappointed when we arrived back to collect our bags and encountered much the same attitude. Nearly no eye contact, barely 3 words spoken, and a very disinterested feeling. Felt like a burden to get our bags - half expected a sigh about the request, honestly. Not sure if this particular agent was having an off day or just a foul person, but certainly didn't leave us wanting to hurry back.
Bottom Line: Even booking well ahead and getting a better than average price, the stay wasn't worth it. The lack-luster experience and obvious non-attention to details like the twin beds and ignoring the "not highway side" request was topped with the single least interested desk agent we've ever encountered. Dressing up a 2 star experience in 5 star prices and attitude doesn't cut it. Our next trip to Seattle we'll be staying elsewhere.

title_masked: Don't stay here until the protests stop
text_masked:
My mum and I stayed here in June 2012.
PROS:
Great location, friendly staff, nice rooms (although the bathroom is bigger than the rest of the room, and the windows provide NO sound barrier to the street outside).
CONS:
The hotel is undergoing some kind of ownership change or something - in any case, every morning at 7am protestors stand outside and form a picket line for one hour. On top of the awful noise that they make, they actually harrassed me and made me feel really uncomfortable and unsafe when I was trying to load my car with our luggage.

title_masked: Friendly Staff But Hotel is Poorly Maintained
text_masked:
Pros: The staff was super friendly -- I'll give them that. And the airport shuttle was convenient. Room was clean and the wifi worked well. 
Cons: Phone did not work; TV remote did not work (until I reprogrammed it): AC was weak and took 3 hours to cool down the room: and the elevator was out of service.
It's one thing to "lack" amenities, it's quite another when the amenities don't work. Was inexpensive so I guess I should not expect the Ritz. Would not stay there again.

title_masked: Pleasant enough service, difficult for hotel to compete with others
text_masked:
Stayed for one night at the Indianapolis Hilton. The location is great, near all the major restaurants and sights in downtown Indy. It is very accessible by the freeway and there is plenty of nearby public parking if you don't want to pay the steep hotel parking fee.
The lobby is large, well-lit, and welcoming and there are two nice spots attached to the hotel for a nice meal or drink.
Check in is efficient and the staff is friendly.
The worst part of the hotel (and why I would probably choose another) is the room. Yes, the hotel is a little older, but my room on the 10th floor did not have a serious window. The room felt like a cell block because the only "window" was a piece of glass that was 1foot wide and maybe 8 ft high. The room felt dark, cold, and unwelcoming. I understand that some hotels in Manhattan may have small windows, but this room should be taken out of the rotation and used as a storage room. I can't comment on the other rooms because I didnt ask for a change, but I feel that if a customer is paying $190/night, he/she should not be put in a room such as this. Perhaps other rooms are nicer, but i didnt have one of those and my experience was soured.
While my room was non-smoking, there was a residual scent of tobacco in the room. The bathroom was dated (but clean) and there was a faint smell of mildew. 
Overall, the location is great, the service is fine, but I was disappointed in the actual room.

The decor of the room was nice and contemporary. But if you look close the room was not cleaned very well. The A/C control looked like there were boogers or something stuck on it. The door jams of the bathroom door and room door has finger prints/marks. Light switches also were gross and had build up of dirt and grime over the years. The blow dryer also had gross markings all over it. I felt very dirty staying here but I had no choice and was very glad it was only for one night. I was in room 701. 
If management is reading this review, please retrain your cleaners. Or at least inspect their work.

My Husband and I stayed at this hotel with our daughter and granddaughter both in their late teens and it was the perfect location from which to see the city.We were within 4minutes walk to times square and 6 minutes from central park.We could also walk to loads of other attractions really easily,ie: 5th avenue,The Rockafella Centre,Radio City, Grand central terminal,and we were also in the heart of Theatre land,so all in all this made our stay perfect!
 There was a great argentinian restaurant practically opposite and just down the side street next to the hotel a lovely Italian restaurant. 
 The hotel itself was very clean and the staff lovely.The rooms were big and linen and towels changed daily.Downstairs in the lobby they had hot drinks available free, day and night,which was great after a day or evening out.We were also able to use internet in the lobby free and this was really useful as we were able to print up all our return flight tickets! A godsend. If there were any negatives it would only be the cooked breakfast which was very rubbery!!, but there was plenty of choose of other cold items cereals, fresh fruit, bagels,pastries etc so that made up for it. Hopefully we will return one day!.

My family had a reservation at this hotel for a non-smoking room. When my husband made the reservation he made it clear that we would be arriving after midnight after flying into Phoenix. When we arrived at 1:30am we were told that our room was a smoking room and was the only room left in the hotel. It smelled like a casino and there was no way we could stay with my husband and daughter having a headache from traveling all day, me being very sensitive to smells and my other daughter had a cold. The front desk clerk had offered to spray something in the room but had no idea of how long it would take to work. We inquired about other hotels in the area but she said they were all full. We decided to leave and drive the 2 hour trip home in the middle of the night. What an inconvenience!
My family was in the hotel business for forty years, and I have a feeling I know what happened. Someone else checked into the smoking room that did not have a non-smoking room reserved. After they complained, the front desk staff decided to rent our room to them and let the night auditor deal with us when we arrived much later. Why didn't the housekeeping staff try to get the room smelling better during the day or anyone else once they realized they would have to place a non-smoking reservation in a smoking room? I left my contact information and asked for the general manager to call us but never heard from her.
I think this property is poorly managed. Before leaving I used the restroom off the lobby. It was a mess. I do not recommend this property and will not try staying here again.

I stayed at this hotel for 4 days/3 nights to attend a conference. Suffice it to say, I was happy when it came time to leave. There is no question that the hotel public areas are beautiful, providing opulence, elegance, and first-class presentation. However, that is where the impressiveness ends. My colleague and I both suffered similar experiences, experiences that are not consistent with the first-class expense and expectation associated with this hotel. First, when we arrived, one elevator door was broken, leaving only one elevator to serve one side of this immense hotel. It took three tries before there was enough room for us and our luggage to get on the car, as conference attendees were on and riding up from lower levels. Unfortunately, that became the problem throughout the stay: not enough elevator service to satisfactorily provide transport for the sheer number of people in the hotel. Getting on the elevator on its first pass was a rare joy - but not really a joy. The elevators, though regal because of wood paneling, are not well ventilated (which makes riding like a sardine with other passengers a less than pleasant experience), and are not well lit (rather than providing "mood lighting," they are just down-right dark). It became a joke among many passengers. If you are claustrophobic or actually are here for business and need to get somewhere within a reasonable period of time, these elevators make it an unwanted experience. Room service is a joke. While the food is excellent and the people who bring it are professional and pleasant, DO NOT order room service if you have anything planned for that day. It just never comes. I ordered ice cream and coffee at 10:30 pm one evening, was promised it would be up in 10-15 minutes, and it arrived 1 hour and 20 minutes later! The same level of (slow) service was afforded on all other room service orders I made (one lunch, one dinner, and one breakfast)- they never arrive when promised, consistently take well more than an hour to arrive (even during non-peak dining hours), and make it absolutely impossible to be able to eat and still have enough time to get to whatever meetings you have planned. Other things happened, too, that, though little, were problems that should not be had in a first-class establishment: one lamp knob was broken, forcing me to have to use one of my make-up appliances to turn it so I could turn it on, the batteries in my TV remote were nearly dead (I got up to change the channel or turn on/off the TV each time), and the iron was cheap and small and dribbled water constantly (ruined a shirt). If you come here for business, bring your own iron - while mine did not work well, my colleague's iron had uncontrollable heat settings (again, cheap irons), resulting in her burning (and ruining) one of her suits. While at the conference, we also were in need of help with something associated with the conference. The manager (?banquet manager?) said he would look into it, thought he may not be able to help, but would be back and definitely would let us know either way - he never returned. The bellmen and doormen are variably helpful - some are absolutely delightful, others hate their jobs and the people they are serving. The host ignored me and my business compatriates on two occasions, making us stand and wait to be seated without even acknowledging our presence (in a near empty restaurant for about 5-10 minutes each time). I do want to add, though, that, once seated, the wait staff themselves in the restaurant are excellent (must give credit where credit is due!). The front desk staff is excellent as well, being attentive, friendly, and impeccably professional. But, the elevators, the always late room service, the broken lamp and dead remote, the disinterested management level individual, the (often) unhelpful bell/door men, and the various other little things (all too numerous to mention - again, it all adds up after awhile) bespeak a hotel that may look grand, but definitely is not. If you want to see the best part of the hotel (foyer, restaurant, ballrooms), then walk in the front door and look around. Then, turn around and stay somewhere else - there are plenty of other hotels in the area with better amenities and service, many of which that will also, despite their superior offerings, actually cost less, too! It was disappointing.

I am at the hotel right now and I have to say its the smallest room/bathroom I have ever been in and I travel every week. When I entered the room, I was very surprised at how small the room was and I am supposed to automatically get an "upgraded room" at check in given my status with Marriott. In this room, there was only enough space for ONE person to walk around the bed without hitting the dresser on the left of the bed, the desk at the bottom of the bed, and the air condition unit on the right side of the bed. Dont let the armoire door hit you in the face! The bathroom was even worse. there is a small shower(no bath tub), next to a small sink, next to the toilet and the toilet barely has enough room to sit given the location of the toilet paper uolder. Again, there's only enough room for one person to stand in front of the sink. if you bend your head over the sink to say wash your face, the top of your head hits the protruding mirror box. Once you start washing your face, water splatters all over your body, and feet. There's no avoiding getting wet all over. There's just no wiggle room! Now, don't get me wrong. I am not a complainer but I felt claustrophobic the whole time I was there. This was the first trip, that I will be glad to be checking out of the room at the end of the trip. The bed was comfortable and that was the only good thing about our room. There is no access to ice, & you have to call for it every night. The lobby is very nice. The rest of the hotel is very nice. The staff is very nice and helpful. I will not be going back to this hotel when I travel back to New York.

title_masked: Cab it if you have a conference at the convention center
text_masked: I booked this hotel because of its proximity to the conference center. However when I arrived, I was told my king bed was not available due to my booking through a 3rd party. What does that mean? I booked through Expedia as most people do. The person at the front desk had no customer skills to keep the customer happy. They offered nothing for the inconvenience. Once I got to my room, it was dingy and obviously needed to be renovated. The closet was a drape hung across the closet. This is a how many star hotel? At this price, I expected a better room. Please do yourself a favor and don’t make the mistake I made. Book at another hotel along the Miracle Mile and cab it to the convention site. For food, you're stuck with the hotel bar and an overpriced restaurant .There is absolutely nothing in the area. Chicago's a great city - unfortunately I didn't see much of it until I transferred to another hotel after my convention. Next time I'll get a more central hotel and take a taxi.

title_masked: trains at night will wake you
text_masked:
This hotel was unwisely built next to an EXTREMELY LOUD train station and trolley station. The staff provide earplugs, but forget it. 
Yes, the property is clean. But the train...prepare to not sleep when the trains go by, HONKING their horns.

title_masked: Starting to show wear - lives mostly on convention
text_masked:
This is on the Riverwalk - if it is your first time in San Antonio and on the Riverwalk, you will likely be thrilled - and be happy with the Westin. But if it is not your first visit, there are much better properties there. The Mokessa, the Hyatt, and the Drury are far better properties.
To begin, the curbside is a mess - the bellmen do not do a very good job of managing the checkin and checkout traffic. They are likely the worst I have seen in this city. The check in process is fair but not that friendly. (Please keep in mind as you read this review, know that I have hosted 7 meetings at this hotel over the past 8 years. It has clearly gone downhill.)
The rooms are starting to show wear and tear. Even though the week I was there with two meeting groups and they were doing touch-up painting, other areas show wear.
The restaurant and bar on the Riverwalk has horrific and slow service. It is interesting to note that on two consecutive nights two different hostesses did not really care if we were seated or not.
Housekeeping is fair. The amenities have gone downhill - again, it seems clear to me that the hotel is living off its convention and meeting business.
Meeting services were below average; service slow; caddy tables not bussed frequently enough; lunches very mediocre.
While it has been a good deal in the past, I think it is worth trying new hotels.
Once again, if this is your first trip to San Antonio and the Riverwalk, you will not have a basis for comparison. The Westin has become like the Marriott Riverwalk - full of itself, busy enough to turn a good profit and maintain a high occupancy, and yet quite mediocre and three star at best.

Stay at the Canterbury for a convention in August 2012. Had an issue at check in with the hotel billing my American Express upfront. I can understand the $50.00 a day for " incidentals " but my credit card was billed for the full amount as well. Stayed at the Hyatt Orange County several months ago and was billed at the end of the stay. The Hyatt did hold several hundred dollars for incidentals as well. Curious why this " boutique " hotel required $1200.00 up front. When we got home the $250.00 for incidentals was refunded. Staff had no explanation for why I had to pay in advance. I did not have a bank or debit card but an American Express credit card. I have never experienced this with any other hotel or resort. Staff was very indifferent to my complaint which put a very bad taste in my mouth from the beginning. Will not be back or recommend this hotel.

Looking at its website you would be forgiven for mistaking The Shoreham for a decently priced, good quality boutique hotel. We should all send congratulatory notes to the web designers. I imagine it was the same team that faked the Apollo 11 lunar landing, such was the level of deception. Look, it is a conveniently placed hotel and is not a hell-hole, but by the same token neither is it presenting itself (or charging itself) as an economy option. Rooms are tiny, dark and either very hot or freezing cold. I have yet to find any natural light and emerge blinking into the daylight upon exit from the place each time. The staff are clearly not happy, motivated souls who live for customer service, perhaps they just need a hug, but perhaps they also need to move on and find a career that fulfils them more. The place is tired and rather poor. It wouldnt take a lot to fix it, a little bit of sympathetic refurbishment from a designer that actually cared for humans rather than purely aesthetic, clever light management, a menu over-haul, comfortable beds and a staff change and you would be back in business. The cockroaches were pleasant however and the wifi was free. Whoop whoop.
Very comfortable,clean,nice bathroom. The view and proximity to Seaport area was so worth the price. Across parking lot to the T station. Walking distance to Cruise Terminal.

Do not be fooled by the Marriot name. The motel is NOT Marriot quality. As soon as we entered the room I realized the closet door was falling off the track. There were marks on the walls, dust on the ceilings from the vents, and the rooms were not updated. Wi-fi is $12.95 per 24 hour period when most hotels offer it free. It is clean, but NOT what I expected.

Great hotel and service. The staff at this hotel will go out of their way to deliver service that exceeds your expectations. Would definitely stay again, again and again. The night before my departure, my husband called to ask if he could get something special (chocolate) sent to my room with a note. The staff member stated he would take care of and don't worry about it. My husband asked how can I pay you and he responded "no problem" for he will take care of it. He ended up buying a bag of M&M's (my favorite) that made my night so special. 
Wow, what customer service. The conversation and action by the team at the hotel has made it to a life long impression that I will to tell everybody how wonderful the team at the Dallas Forth Worth Holiday Inn was.

Our travel agent managed to get us a good deal for just one night after a cruise that arrived early morning at pier 35. After the usual USA immigration delays, we arrived about 9:30am, but had requested our TA inform them of the early arrival.
The receptionist hardly batted an eyelid when we said that an email had been sent and had a room ready straightaway. The receptionist also supplied a temporary Starwood loyalty card as even though we have been Starwood members for a over a year, we never had a card. 
As others have said, the lifts are a bit slow and the hotel layout is a bit confusing until you have been to and from your room a couple of times. The room was advertised as for a Starwood prreferred guest, was clean and spacious, yet the beds were only doubles and not Queen or King, which is unusual.
Food in the coffee bar appeared a bit pricey, but there is a 711, Subway and other eateries close by.
Great location as the Hop On Hop Off bus office and terminus is less than 100 yards away and the waterfront not much further.
Piers 39 and 45 are within easy walking distance.
No refrigerator in the room is poor at this price and the rooms are not double glazed. Our room wasn't dark enough as the Roman blinds let in far too much light and there were lights outside.
At $25, we decided that breakfast was too expensive.
We parked our luggage and the pleasant concierge also booked our airport shuttle, which arrived on time at 6:15pm. We didn't use the pool but we did sit outside late afternoon until the shuttle pick up, in a sunny area primarily for smokers, adjacent to reception. There is an outdoor gas fire for each of the four seating areas which is pleasant enough. We weren't troubled by smoke drifting across either.
The important question as always, is "would we stay again". Given the ideal location, the answer would probably be yes.

This hotel was terrible value for money. They charge something like 300+ US$. They give you a tiny cubby hole of a room. The room does not have any closet so you are forced to live out of a suitcase. The aircon controls are fake – everything is controlled centrally so you may alternately freeze and sweat. When I came back from dinner on the first night, I found that the AC was not working. On calling reception, I got some ‘We’ll take care of it’ sort of reply. After 15 minutes, I went downstairs to complain and the reception said that the ‘AC Maintenance’ person was busy and would shortly be putting the AC on – 15 minutes to put on an AC switch??? They also do not have a breakfast area – ostensibly because ‘there are many restaurants’ in the area. While the hotel and the room was relatively clean, that is the only positive. I should have checked the ratings on Tripadvisor instead of looking solely at Expedia. I would not recommend this hotel to anybody, no matter how desperate.
A.K.Mondal
Mumbai

title_masked: Nice but needs to iron out some kinks
text_masked: This hotel is brand new and is very nice and clean. The property itself is great. Clean, good layout, very inviting, etc. I won't go so far as to say that the staff sucked, because they were all nice, but none of them were very good at their jobs. Service at the bar/restaurant was so slow, particuarly for the fact that it wan't very busy. Nobody seemed to know when/if the restaurant would be open. I felt like I wanted to like the place, but it was hard to at times. The pool was closed for maintenance or something, our refrigerator in our room didn't work, etc. I guess I would give the place another shot because it is very new/clean, when the pool opened it was nice, the workout room is nice, the restaurant/bar outside of the service was good, parking was convenient, etc. In sum, a nice hotel that needs to get it's "stuff" together.

My husband and I took our 2 young children to Chicago this weekend and we stayed at the W Hotel - Lake Shore (booked through Hotwire.com). A pleasant stay - the location was ideal (we had a great view of Navy Pier), and our 2 double bed room was comfy for our family. Unfortunately, the lack of attention to the details were immediately apparent: the room had poor ventilation (windows were condensed with steam from the shower for most of the weekend) and had a faint smell of cigarette smoke, there was not directory in regards to room/hotel amenities, the condition of the pool was not ideal (pool water was salty and the pool area smelled faintly of formaldehyde) and the TV monitors in the exercise room had poor reception. Obviously, this was a deal on Hotwire, so for what we paid, what we got was above average, but I would never pay full price for this hotel after our weekend.

title_masked: Noisy, some problems, but - good location and price
text_masked:
I stayed at this location with my husband and toddler this past week. To get to the nitty gritty (!): 
Negatives: we were given key cards that didn't work so we had to go back to the counter and get new ones (this happened two or three times during our one week stay here!), on the air conditioner unit we found someone's toe-nail clippings (yuck), and the floor felt like it wasn't vacuumed (my feet got dirty from walking barefooted). Also, this hotel was really noisy and I didn't sleep well because of it. Several nights we'd wake up during the night to people making noise in the hallway. In the mornings, house-keeping would start knocking on doors and in a loud voice announce "HOUSEKEEPING!" (I honestly thought at first it was someone pulling a prank on someone, but we checked and it was the actual housekeeping staff doing this) - what's worse is that this would be heard at 7am!! Much too early in my opinion. Finally, we had a city-view room and because the hotel is so close to the highway we heard a lot of traffic noise.
Positives: room has free WIFI, mini-fridge, microwave and a safe. Hotel has pool on-site which is a must in that heat! (It was 104 F when we visited!) It's nice they offer free breakfast, although it consists only of bagels, muffins, and apples, and several times when we went downstairs (around 9am) the breakfast food was already gone. The location is within walking distance to the Alamo and downtown Riverwalk which is great. Parking fee here is less than hotels in the area, which is another benefit.

I stayed here for a few night while in business in DC. The hotel was nice enough, but could use an update. I found the decor to be old and dated. I've stayed in some really nice Homewood Suites such as the one in Baltimore, and this one is not up to that one's standard.

I picked this hotel since the conference I was attending was also at this venue When you first walk into the hotel it seems very luxurious with lots of marble, huge ceilings, artwork etc, but my room in Harbor Tower was entirely the opposite. When we got to our room the first thing we noticed was a water stain on the ceiling, a mildew odor, and a very, very wet patch of carpet. We would have been OK with ignoring it if we hadn't had stained sheets when we attempted to get into our bed. The next morning my husband went to the front desk to complain about the wet carpet and he was simply told that there was construction happening on the floor above us and they had overbooked the hotel so there was nothing they could do. The mildew was starting worsen my allergies so the next morning I spoke with the concierge and she was very pleasant. She offered to comp us a night stay in the room as well as offer to send someone up to investigate and clean the patch of carpet, hopefully removing the mildew odor. No one came.
I came down again the next morning and pointed out a few extra things I found wrong in the room including someone else's hair still attached to the hair dryer, a mold/mildew spot in the corner of the bathroom, and the rusting door frame of the bathroom. Thankfully, despite being overbooked, they were at least able to relocate us (although I feel quite bad for the folks that ended up in our room that night). The second room was MUCH better and in Seaport Tower. It actually smelled clean, was clean, had dry carpet and it had a lovely view. With it being a corner room we had 3 windows to enjoy the view with. The remainder of our stay was better and the buffet at Lael's was quite delicious, but during the first 3 days of the stay, quality of the room and the construction noise occurring above the room left something to be desired. 
I am appreciative of the concessions that were made by the hotel in an attempt to right the situation, but despite the high touting of the renovated rooms, I would be hesitant to revisit them for another stay without a business reason to do so.

I've stayed in a few Embassy Suites across the country and I would say that this one is right on par with the others and with what you would expect from a family-friendly hotel. The staff was excellent and super friendly (special shout out to Dwayne, the bellman, who spoke to us every single time we passed him). We stayed July 4 - 7 and there was some sort of Irish Dance competition going on. We spent a lot of time on Thursday and Friday waiting for elevators that weren't full by the time they reached us on the 12th floor. Our room was average and clean, but the pillows completely suck and gave me the worst neck ache. We went for the manager's reception the first night and after waiting 20 minutes in line for a drink...decided it wasn't worth it and hit up Dominick's across the street so we could just make our own cocktails in the room. Overall, this is an average hotel with friendly staff and a great location, but prepare to wait for elevators, drinks and breakfast during busier time periods.

I've stayed at this property 4 times in the last 2 months and was not overly impressed.
On each of the first 3 stays I booked a rate that included breakfast and each time the front desk indicated that it was not included in my rate and only included it after I showed them the reservation details from the Marriott website which indicated breakfast was included. Even after getting them to correct this upon checkin I was still denied breakfast on one occassion even after the restaurant inquired with the front desk, so beware that you get everything included in your rate.
Other than my issues with the breakfast, the hotel is acceptable, but not exceptional.
The Good: Nice lobby area; staff was friendly; comfortable and nicely appointed rooms; great internet speeds
The Bad: HVAC is loud; try to get a room away from the main road (Tower Rd.) because road noise can be heard in the room; small fitness center; bathroom counter is small
Overall not a bad hotel, but I believe there are better alternatives in the area.

Great Location!!! Elevators need to be brought into the 21st century. USC WiFi is Awesome. Rooms need to be Remodeled. Rooms are low end quality, Mold around showers, Ripped Chairs, Noisy outdated A/C unit. Clogged shower drain. Vending and ice machine didnt work. Room Service Breakfast is average. McKay's and Rosso Pizza are good.

We stayed in this hotel 3 weeks ago and I have to say the staff are the worst I ever encountered. Am i asking too much for a thank you, how are you ? etc? Every staff memeber we met bar one was rude and in no way friendly. 
The bar menu for what you get is over priced and the quality of the food is not great. We eat there once and decided not to again..
Yes the hotel is located in a very good location but after that there isnt really any positives. it seems the motto is try to get as much money from the guest as possible while showing them as little respect as possible! Overall we spent 3 days there and I must say it was a major disappointment. If you are going for a romantic break then avoid this hotel !!

title_masked: Stiff robotic front desk staff that does not greet you as you walk by
text_masked: The spectacular room $250 and the regular rooms $189 are exactly the same except the spectacular is on a higher floor, the view is nothing special. Rooms are very average. Be prepared to have a hold of $250.00 on your credit card for incidental charges. Valet parking is a ridiculous $37 per day, plus tax. comes out to be about $45 a night, with that kind of charge you will have no interest in tipping the valet staff. You can walk through the lobby pass the front desk and hear a pin drop, no greeting and eye contact, everyone's eyes are on a computer screen. I think the only greeting i got was from the guy in the lobby marketing Acura SUVs. FYI lots of homeless folks in the downtown area. I you are reading this and you are the General Manager......the take away is pay attention to customer service.

For years the Empire Hotel, across the street from Lincoln Center, was a seedy, rundown venue. In those days, it deserved the comment I once heard from American composer Morton Gould: "I don't mind the cockroaches, I just wish they wouldn't charge you double occupancy for them." But the hotel closed for a few years, was rumored to be converted to condominiums when the real estate bust hit, and it was eventually taken over by the World Hotels chain and completely renovated. It is now clean, elegantly appointed, and continues to benefit from being across the street from Lincoln Center.
Unfortunately, the renovation did not include re-building the rooms. They are tiny, as are the bathrooms - where there is barely enough room to change your mind. The poorly designed shower makes it impossible to test the water temperature before being subjected to it -- unless you are a contortionist. You must stand under it to turn it on. The shower also has only a half-door, so you must get the bathroom floor wet. But, on the positive side, for its small size the bathroom has very good shelf space for your toiletries and medicines.
There is no easy-chair in the room (no space for it) - a bed, desk and desk chair, and a few feet of floor space to navigate your way around. This would be acceptable, perhaps, if the price weren't so high - I paid $399 for a room there recently.
If you're willing to pay the price, and need to be close to Lincoln Center, then it is acceptable. The service is very good, the folks are nice and efficient, and, as I said, it is clean and elegant.

We stayed 3 nights with our 20 months daughter. The hotel is ok, clean, but considering the high price paid, the room and bathroom were small and nothing special about them. The soundproofing of the rooms is bad, we could hear the people next door and in the corridor at night. The service is good though and the location is great, walking distance to everything. I recommend The Thinking Cup for breakfast, a short walk from the hotel. Next time in Boston, we will try another hotel in the same area.

title_masked: Pleasant 2 night stay at the Hilton Garden Inn
text_masked:
We stayed here for two nights on the last leg of our honeymoon from the 15th-17th September 2012 and it was very pleasant.
Rooms and decor basic but comfortable and the 2 employees on the Reception desk Anthony Pham and Helena were lovely, helpful and friendly ( especially on our checking out day).

I stayed here for a convention in the Moscone Center in late August. It is a 10 minute walk through a nice area (across Market St.). I was in room 810, which wasn't big, but sufficent. New flat screen, desk, coffee maker, safe, nice comfortable kingsize bed and pillows, good size bath room, smallish tub, great WiFi coverage although somewhat slow at times. Carpets, paint etc. all lookd fine although the cupboard looked a little worn to me. Only drawback in the room was that it was a little on the dark side (just one, relatively, small window), and the fact that it had a door to an adjoining room, which meant you quite clearly could hear the neighbours. It didn't bother me, as they weren't noisy. The gym is very small and only has one treadmill, one bike, one cross trainer, weights and one of those multi-functional-thingies. All new and in good condition, but if you want more, there's a real gym on the same block, which you can buy day-passes for at the reception for 12USD. The receptionists were nice and helpful. They have a wine-tasting in the afternoons, but if you really appreciate wine, you will probably be disappointed :-/ But I guess it is some sort of attempt of compensating for not having a bar, and as such I like the idea. They don't have any restaurant either, but there is a Japanese/Mexican restaurant next door (weird combination) which they recommended. It must open quite late as I never saw it open in the mornings (before 8AM when I left. Next to the hotel there is "Bread and Cocoa" which is coffee shop where I had my breakfasts, which were great. There is also a Starbucks up the street. 
If you enjoy a run, it is less than 1km to the sea/piers, where you can get some nice long and very beatiful runs uninterrupted by traffic. As I was in town for a big conference, prices were very high (for all the hotels I checked) and I paid around 400USD per day. If I come back, and the prices aren't jacked up due to big events, I would stay here again, but at any other time of the year, I would never pay that much for a 3,5 star hotel. Supply and demand, I guess.

title_masked: Not worth what I paid, but nice
text_masked:
I stayed here with a few friends for the 2012 Ohayocon. It was convenient that they had a shuttle running from the hotel to the convention center and back, however, I don't think that this was planned by the hotel, and it was at the furthest possible corner of the hotel away from everyone else. I got the distinct impression that they were trying to hide all the anime nerds away from the rest of the hotel.
Our trip was in February and it was very very cold, so waiting outside of a locked outside far away back door was not convenient at all, when the shuttle could have pulled into the drive through right near the lobby and it would've been much nicer.
Having said that, the beds were nice but we were placed in a single instead of a double room (though I called before to guarantee it was a double) and we were given a cot because they could not move us out of the room.
For close to $250 bucks a night, I expected at least free breakfast, but their 3 egg omelets were $12 dollars! I've had much more for a fraction of the price.
The staff was considerate and helped us out a lot, I know a lot of the circumstances that we were put in could not have been solved at that point in time by the front desk staff.
Overall, I would say this hotel was not a good value for the amount of money I paid for it.

I've stayed in this hotel a couple different times and I'm always surprised how poor it is given the Hilton brand. The lobby area is nice but very cramped. The rest of the hotel is in very poor condition. Carpet looks like it was installed in the 1980's. The rooms wer also very disappointing. The doors to the hallway are very poorly built with large gaps near the floor that allow you to hear practically everything that goes on outside your room throughout the night. My room was connected to two other rooms and the insulation between the two was terrible. I could hear one individual snoring so loudly it sounded as if he was in my room. The food was terrible. I ate one evening at the Boardwalk and should have taken a hint when only two other guests were dining there. While the airport is very conveniently located for flights into Houston Hobby, there isn't much available on that side of Houston so you end up driving for even a decent meal. Overall, very unimpressed and unless I'm required to go for business, I will never stay at this hotel.

title_masked: Bad experience made me change my mind about this place
text_masked:
I have been using Staybridge hotels in various cities in the USA and been very impressed with services and suites to the stage that I became Platinum Member.
The last experience in Memphis was the worst! I don't think I will stay there again nor would I recommend this place.
The room smelled with smoking even though we were promised non-smoking room.
The bed linen looked old, my wife brought linen from outside.
On the third day, we were attacked with large cockroaches in the living room. I informed the front desk who verified similar problems, the room was sprayed afterward.
The worst part, on the last two days, the bathroom produced a terrible smell after 10PM, to the point that we had to avoid the bathroom during these hours, the staff could not fix the problem the following day

title_masked: Wish I could have stayed longer.
text_masked: I was only in town for one night and stayed at the Renaissance hotel. On a busy street so be careful getting out of your car, but at least the valet was on top of it all. The lobby was a bit smaller than I would have expected but it was very bright and ornate, quite beautiful. The staff was very nice and the concierge was very helpful with restaurant recommendations. My room was a bit out of the way of the elevator and a little difficult to find. The hallways are numbered rather awkwardly and had to keep looking at all the doors. I felt like maybe my room was in a different building but eventually found it. My room was a good sized room and felt very spacious. I had two full beds but my coworker had a queen of the same sized room with a seating area. The bed was very comfortable and I just sank into the mattress. There is an actual floorlength, three foot wide mirror in the entryway which would be on any lady's wish list. The bathroom was quite ornate with a nice sized tub, couldn't wait to soak a little. It was close enough to the visitor attractions, but there is not much else in the immediate vicinity. Overall quite a nice stay. I'm sure this is a good price for DC, but I don't like to pay this much on a vacation.

title_masked: I would stay here again and again
text_masked: A gem of a hotel located near Seattle Univerisity and Pill Hill. I stayed here alone for two nights, and loved it. The staff were very warm and generous. A glass of wine was waiting at check in, hand the rooms were clean, well appointed, and the beds comfortable. It is an old hotel, so the elevator is small (which is charming) and the plumbing a little slow to bring up the hot water (which is a shame as they must waste a lot of water.) They have a restaurant which I did not go to because it was more a meat lovers place. But the lounge was quiet and comfortable. I sat by the fire and ordered wine and read and just had a wonderful time all by myself.

title_masked: Terrible Service, Terrible Billing, Terrible Experience
text_masked:
Booked correctly, got confirmed but was put into a different room because they send someone else to my room. I had to chase people to move from the two twin bed room to the king bed one that I reserved and that happened after I begged for it and late in the afternoon. I was offered with "a breakfast" to compensate for all the misunderstandings but, they ended up charging it to my corporate card.
Not a good choice if you're attending AdTech or if a corporate client. Stay at the W or other more serious option.

My family spent the night in Chicago during spring break. The staff was great to us and our kids. They had a goodie bag for the kids when we arrived with a scavenger hunt that they loved. The indoor pool and sundeck on the 17th floor provided great views and fun. We enjoyed our stay and all the amenities.

This motel was the worst i have ever seen seriously they should not operate this place in the condition that it is in. When we checked into the room the garbage was full and they place it in the closet, the cloth that they use to wash or try to wash the bathroom with was hanging up in the bathroom. the bathroom was very dirty from previous user the shampoo bottle that they uused was still in the bathroom with the left over soap. Soap scum was on the wall tiles, the shower curtain look like it has not been clean in months, stain on the rugs the bedroom was smelling very musty the ceiling was hanging with watermarks all over it. Simply put the room was filthy could not sleep on those bed linens went out and bought linens to spread ontop of the comforters they had on the bed. We had an allergic reaction the whole time we were there. The front desk area is nicely done but that is it. Not worth the stay even though its close yo the base. this is a place for prostitutes for a couple hours obsolutely horrible. its not even worth $1 a night.

title_masked: The bad review are correct in most respects - please read.
text_masked:
I stayed for 10 nights - it was prepaid so the front desk will not refund.
Property stolen from room - on the only day in 10 that a maid came to change the sheets - I mean the rooms are never serviced, how bad is that! You have to get towels and soap from reception.
The lifts break down often.
While the location is great - spare a little more $$ and get something else close by - I would have doen this if I had not pre paid - you have been warned!! I suspect the so called good reviews on here about the Carter are dummy reviews by the hotel, it really is that bad.

I stayed there the past week. It is on the far end of the riverwalk and close to restaurants, bars,shops and the Alamo. Other plusses include clean room,plenty of towels, friendly cleaning and maintenance staff and extremely helpful porter(he helped us get to all the best restaurants and shopping). Negatives are unfriendly front desk, unavailability of refridgerators, worn decor(ceiling was peeling in four places in our room),and absolutely horrible food in the restaurant.

title_masked: Great Hotel and Location; Poor Pool/Exercise Area
text_masked:
Hard to find a better location: just a block from where the airport train stops (Westlake train station and bus tunnel under Nordstrom's, from which you can get almost anywhere), across from the Westlake shopping center and monorail hub, across the street from a pharmacy which sells snacks and minimal groceries, and only a short 15-minute walk to Pike's Place market and the waterfront.
This is a large hotel. I was here for a conference and spent most of my time on the three conference floors, so for business travelers here's my take on that: many rooms, some huge some small, which makes this a perfect place for such events. Room setup and service was great. My only complaint is that a few times the doors between room dividers (in the Cascade rooms) didn't close properly, so it was difficult to hear over noise from adjoining sessions.
The guest rooms were great, and the "heavenly beds" were indeed heavenly. The in-house restaurant was ok, but not great. I ate from the buffet Sunday morning before I flew out--a very large selection (scrambled eggs, fresh pancakes, plentiful fruit, and rolls, bacon, sausage, yogurt, etc), but the eggs were dry and overcooked. Adult buffet price was $19.00.
The exercise room was small and cramped. It contained barbells, an exercise ball and three different weight machines. You wouldn't want to spend much time in here, especially if there were more than one other person. The pool was a disappointment; small and so shallow at one end that you hit your hands/feet when swimming laps. And it tasted/smelled salty and a little disgusting. The temperature in both the pool and the spa varied widely from day to day--one day it was so cold it was unbearable to swim in. And there was plaster falling off the pillar at the west end, which no one cleaned up during my entire 4-day stay and which thus got tracked around the pool.
But aside from the pool problem, this was a great hotel

title_masked: Rethinking of reserving this hotel (especially via hotwire.com) !!!
text_masked:
I was ordered this hotel through hotwire.com one month in advance and fully paid it.
I got a confirmation from hotwire and the hotel.
Suprisingly, when I had arrived to the hotel there were no available rooms and I got a room in a lousy hostel on the other side of the street.
To make the long story short, i paid 140$ per night, got hotel which is cost 66$ per night.
Hotwire were willing to refund me with a redicilus amount of 25$.
I would not recommend having no buiseness with both horwire.com and this hotel !!!

always love the hampton inns , this one had a very good review , our room was smaller (no microwave nor refrig and pool area very small and not shaded (101 degree weather ) large opened breakfast area and computer space did not see many of their staff as in other inns but all were friendly and helpful ! hotel was clean and fresh per usual no real complains ! (we used hotels.com and got great rates on room ! )
we were attending a family b/day party so we were happy to drive up to ft worth from houston and have a clean and decent place to stay including morning breakfast. The next day we toured the city a bit, stockyards and the cowgirl museum, shopped and even got to go to a Sam Moons which is a great place for costume jewelry, handbags etc at reasonable prices .
it was a long ride back and forth but rented a car locally thru enterprise car rental and again a great rate and that was well worth it ! 
we will always recommend the hampton inn and now will include enterprise car rentals as another one of our favorites that we can count on !

This is my first time ever staying at a Candlewood Suites Hotel. Well I stayed here only for one night and let me tell you. I enjoyed my stay and I would stay here again if I ever had the chance. Close to shopping at the Galleria Mall and other shops.

I came to Philadelphia to visit my daughter who is a college student at Swarthmore and brought my teenage son so we could explore Philadelphia. I decided to stay in the Old City and selected the Omni based on other travelers' reviews - mainly for location and moderate price. Great selection - the hotel itself is terrific, the staff is super helpful and friendly, and the location is perfect. Obviously it's in the heart of the historic area, but it is also very easy to walk to almost everywhere in the main part of the city. Over the course of two days, we explored from Penn's Landing all the way over to the Art Museum, center city, China Town, the Italian Market, Society Hill, and many other destinations in addition to the historic sites - all on foot. 
The Omni was top rate and everything about our experience was great. The rooms are plush and has all the qualities you would expect in a high-end hotel. Getting in and out of the city from here is actually pretty easy too. Parking was pricey at $37/night for valet parking, but it was no hassle and probably worth the premium given that parking is hard to come by in the central part of the hotel. Overall a great hotel and I would definitely stay here again.

title_masked: Buyer beware of customer satisfaction policies
text_masked:
I'll be as fair as I can. Lovely lobby, great location. We're currently staying for the week, but thought to get our warning out early to potentially save other people their hard-earned money.
The other reviews are accurate - small rooms, loud AC... we were prepared for this. We were not prepared for mattresses with no box springs (just wood supports = extremely hard beds), lumpy pillows like rolled up socks, and *vibration* of the bed from the loud permanent AC, which is inches from your head, given the size of these rooms, and earplugs don't stop this. Unfortunately, the warning to those considering a "boutique" hotel is that, unlike any other hotel you may have stayed at, payment is NOT due at checkout, and you cannot simply leave and go elsewhere if you are unsatisfied. From their website, carefully buried, emphasis theirs, not mine:
Cancellation Policy:
Cancellation and/or Changes must be received by The Washington Jefferson Hotel by NOON hotel time at least 72 hours prior to arrival. No Refunds, No Changes and No Cancellations. FULL PAYMENT AT TIME OF BOOKING. .
Reservations must be made with a valid credit card or the hotel will not confirm. 
So, if you don't like your room, your stay, or your trip, go jump. Whaddya want? We'll take your money first, and then nuts to you! This is New York!
Read the fine print, folks.

title_masked: Many issues: Do not book the hotel through third party.
text_masked:
I stayed at Westin, Chicago River North for 4 nights for a business trip. I had booked the hotel through a third party website. We were a part of a conference delegates. The check in was fine. However, there were many issues subsequently. I was told that there is no free internet although the conference lodging information mentioned free internet in the room at this hotel. When asked for a clarification, the front desk told me that since the room was booked through a third party, this offer was not available to me. My other colleagues, who stayed at the other Westin, less than a mile away were offered free internet while they had also booked through a third party. So, I guess this hotel follows its own rules.
The quality of the beds was not up to the mark of other Westin properties and these were easily the worst beds of any business hotels I have stayed at. The refrigerator was not working well. The shower knobs in the bathroom rusted and only one of the two heads of "heavenly showers was working" and the water pressure was extremely poor. I expressed these concerns at the end of my stay to the check out desk. Finally at the end of this all, I see extra charge on my credit card without even an invoice sent to me. I have no idea what these charges are for. The restaurant was decent but serves their Egg-Benedict with fish instead of bacon.Who does that? I would not recommend the hotel, especially if you are booking it through third party. And it is not worth the price offered on the hotel website.

title_masked: "Sex in the City" didn't have it this nice
text_masked: The location is perfect for daily trips to the many local restaurants, shopping and business. The hotel is just small enough to remain personal, including freshly baked cookies delivered to my room every evening, yet large enough to provide a wide range of services. Thank you, Michelle, for the pleasant daily breakfast greetings and to the management for hiring staff who truly care. The accommodations are superb—I love waking up in the Temperpedic bed to a stunning floor to ceiling view of Manhattan. Truly, Sex in the City didn’t have it this good.

We were told the room was going 199$ than when we checked in we were told it was 229. When we finally got to our room, we got a text message from our bank saying we were overdrawn. We found out that without telling us the hotel charged 319. They never mentioned they charge 20% just in case we get room service. we were not planning on room service. They charged us 90$ more than they said they were going too. 90$ more than my husband signed to pay. I do not understand how they could charge and not tell us the actual amount. It ended up making it so we could not go to the Willis Tower because the money was being held. Very disappointed. Also, the lady checking us out forgot to ask us for the room keys. we didn't realize so we had to walk all the back to the hotel since we could not afford a cab. Location was great. The room didn't even have a fridge. The vending machines were right outside our room so we got woken up a few times by other hotel visitors during the night. For the price, I think it was an awful experience.

I've stayed in plenty of hotels...some worse, many better. This one is worth writing about. We arrived on the shuttle after waiting 25 minutes...and the hotel is less than 10 from the airport. Check in was really fast...but that euphoria was short-lived. The room had NO toilet paper on two holders. We later discovered no cups. Then my trip to the hot tub was a big disappointment as the water was pool-warm (maybe 85 degrees). The desk did knock off 5 bucks from our bill, so I was not too unhappy until I returned two days later. THIS time, one of the beds had dirty sheets (human hair and a stain on the sheet), and a broken drapery pull. The wait for a shuttle was over 40 minutes and when it did arrive, it was stuffed full and the driver was extremely rude (replying, "so?" when I said we had been waiting for over a half-hour). We were eventually picked up after 50 minutes. The building is starting to show its age, but the service is what is really poor.

The only good thing I can say about this hotel is the location is ideal.
We are Marriott Elite members and have stayed in Marriott Hotels around the world, 
the staff in this hotel were the most rude and arrogant I have ever had the misfortune to meet.
We booked the one bedroom suite 12 months ago requesting a high floor and quiet room because we would be driving 10 hours from Las Vegas to San Francisco that day, we even phoned the hotel to confrim this.
On arrival there was no valet parking, there were no trollies for all our bags, I unloaded and parked the car, when I returned the valet was taking keys from another guest, apparently space was available the other valet was mistaken, no apology!
My wife the informed me she was offerred no assistance with all our bags.
The room we required had been allocated to another client , we were given a room on the first floor overlooking the street and the waste bins, which were collected at 4-30am. 
When I asked the desk clerk for an alternative room, his response was that none were available, his attitude was we had a room, then he stated if we wished to check out he would only charge us half the room rate.
I advised him that we would check out first thing in the morning.
The room was noisy all night and even with ear plugs we were unable to sleep due to the waste collection and the traffic.
I would add that the morning staff were much more helpful and polite and the deputy manager was full of apologies.
The hotel is basic and very tired, it is in need of a complete facelift and it is not good value for money.
Fortunately we were able to obtain a bay view room at the ARGONAUT HOTEL, just around the corner, which was fabulous and in a differrent class, with polite staff that could not do enough for you.
For a small difference in price I would advise all to stay at a proper hotel the ARGONAUT.

title_masked: Poor service and poor value for money
text_masked:
I stayed at the Mansfield for 4 days and was really disappointed. We stayed in a double double parlour room (one of the more expensive) and it was pokey and very dark - more importantly it wasn't clean. The bedside table and desk were covered in dust and the counterpanes on the beds were filthy. Twice the sheets on my bed had big rips in them. The room also looked out on to the street and was incredibly noisy.
We really struggled with the internet here when we critically needed to get on so would not recommend for anyone on business. The staff were very little help when we asked for help to get on the internet or to move rooms with one notable exception (F&B manager). Throughout the stay staff would look at you blankly when you asked for help and we needed to follow up two or three times for anything to happen.
There are much better hotels in NY at this price bracket - would not recommend.

The greatest virtue of this hotel is its position. It is in Midtown near the Lincoln centre and theatre district. Columbus circle subway only 3 minutes walk away and you can get most places easily from here. Rooms are tiny for the price though thoroughly livable and with everything one needs...I had to move rooms as the street-side was very noisy - the courtyard side of the hotel was better...airconditioning was noisy but effective...wifi included which is great...price is a lot for anywhere else in the world but probably fair for new york...concierge helpful and I liked modern lobby...breakfast is over-priced so better to eat at one of numerous new york cafes around...

The first experience was great...the last two were horrible. I travel for work and know we all have bad days...I get it...but I realize this hotel has spiraled out of control. The management has lost control and it is apparent. 
The staff is all new and nobody has any training. 
Please seek anything else but here. If you think sleeping in the airport is a horrible idea, trust me when I tell you that it is better than staying at the Comfort Suites DIA. The owner is unreasonable and is the only person allowed to make a decision. She treats you like a terrorist and is less than personable.

My wife and I stayed here last week because she had a convention to attend early the next morning. It is right across the street from the convention center and Water Gardens, so you can't get much closer if you are looking for something close by. 
When we called to reserve the room, they quoted my wife $369/night! This hotel is not even close to worth that price. It's very dated and the rooms are what you'd see in any budget hotel. So we complained about the price. Then suddenly, they had a room available for $169. I hate how hotels do that. Always ask for a lower price, because usually you'll get it. I can't stress enough that this hotel is not work $300/night, not even close. But if you can get them close to $100, you'll probably feel OK about it. 
Check in was fast, valet is expensive. Self parking is also expensive. We ate dinner in the hotel restaurant. The food was pretty good, but the service was very slow. The waitress was friendly enough, but she hardly even came by, and we had to keep reminding her of this we needed because she'd forget....ketchup, more water, salsa, etc. Seriously, every single time, she forgot until we reminded her again. I would understand if they were busy, but there were probably about 8 people in the entire restaurant, and most of them were just sitting at the bar, so she didn't even have to handle them. 
If you just need a place to sleep while you go out into the town, or the convention center during the day, it's an OK place. If you want to stay at a nice hotel, I would pick one of the other, nicer ones downtown.

Upon booking my room for one night for myself, my wife and my two kids(age 4yrs and 11months) I was told that a room with two double beds would be reserved. When I checked in the guy at the front desk said all they had left was a king bed with a pull out couch. Pull out couch it was not! It was two foam pads that stack on top of each other to make a couch. When they are pulled together, they resemble anything but a bed. Once we got to the room we realized there were no pillows or linens for this make shift bed but we wanted to go to dinner so we decided to wait till we got back to request them from the front desk. When we walked in the lobby(approx 10:00pm) and requested extra linens/pillows, one of the guys at the desk rudely told me it will be at least 30 minutes before they will be brought to our room. Surprisingly only took about 15 minutes before they showed up at the door. The room itself appeared to be fairly clean...however, we allowed my 11 month old to crawl around on the floor while we got ready for bed and within 10 or so minutes, he legs and feet were absolutely filthy like she had been crawling around in the dirt.
Overall, our stay was failry pleasant. We felt that we should have been compensated in some way for not getting the roomn with two beds we needed/requested. But what can you do? Had we known from the begginning that we were getting a king room, we probably would have brought the pack and play for the baby to sleep in.

I find shopping in that area to be so touristy bourgeois, but we wanted a place under $200 in the city so we could catch the trains and buses to the Shedd and Sears Tower. Mission accomplished, as the 146 bus leaves near there for the museum campus and the Chicago L station is a short five block walk. Nice in that way, but you wind through tons of tourists trying to by happiness at the ridiculously overpriced stores. The suites are quite small. While there is a separate bedroom with un-lockable doors, the living area is tight. The pool is very small for this large of a hotel but offers a really nice view of parts of the city and lake. Parking is 55 bucks a night for valet. We opted for a garage down the street. The location is also nice since it is about 3 blocks from Oak St. Beach on Lake Michigan, which is one of the better areas. We also walked from Navy Pier to the hotel in about 20-25 minutes, so that is a plus. It is a fine hotel for under 200 around there, but the area is so full of shallow consumerism it is sickening.

This was my first trip to NYC in forty years, and we wanted to be close to theaters but not too close to lots of noise and lights. This hotel was perfect. It is within easy walking distance to everything in the theater district as well as museums and shopping and the subway. The rooms were very nice, clean, and comfortable. The beds at Hampton Inn are always comfortable, and these were no exception. I also like for a room to be cool and dark for sleeping, which our room was. Except for one night, the hotel was also very quiet. Unfortunately, some young men decided to have a party in the room next to us one night, and the noise at 2:00 a.m. woke me up; however, I called the front desk and they sent security to the room, which took care of it. The only thing I would not recommend is the breakfast. We only ate the breakfast on the last day, and even though it's free, I have had better breakfasts at other Hampton Inns. Otherwise, I would highly recommend this hotel for a great place to stay in New York City.

This is the second time my husband and I stayed at this La Quinta. The first time was a wonderful stay. No complaints. This time, however was not as enjoyable. I read about the roaches and did not notice any on the first night we stayed here. On the morning of our check out of our two night stay, my husband noticed a small brown roach crawling on the wall and went behind the picture frame. I was glad to be leaving because I don't think I could have stayed another night knowing there were roaches in the room. Other problems, when we arrived we were given keys to a room that had not been cleaned yet by housekeeping. We were immediately offered another room which had been cleaned. It appears that others have written about roaches and yet the hotel management does not take care of the issue. I guess they are not concerned since they are not the ones staying in the rooms. We will not return to this La Quinta. Too bad because we really enjoyed our stay for the most part, but cannot bare the thought of returning due to the unsanitary condition of the hotel.

We stayed at this hotel with a soccer group for a tournament. We were greeted by very efficient and friendly staff at the front desk in a very classy, modern lobby. Then we went to our room. The bed was very uncomfortable and the sofa bed was horrible. The carpeting very badly needed to be vacuumed. The nifty dispensers in the bathroom for shampoo, conditioner and shower gel were empty. The shower curtain was too short to tuck inthe tub to keep a lake from forming on the floor. We set the air on a comfortable temperature and it went there...and then reverted back to the original hot temperature we found it on. And it was very loud. On the plus side, the breakfast that was provided in a meeting room for our group was very decent and the young man who kept it stocked was very pleasant. The rooms were well soundproofed so we didnt hear noise from the other guests or the traffic we could see on the highway that was very close by. And when I asked for more towels, they brought me a huge stack within minutes. Also, there is a Cracker Barrel restaurant across the parking lot.

title_masked: Dumpster pick-up at 7 AM on Sunday morning! Seriously?
text_masked:
This is a decent hotel in a great location, but there are some major problems. First, who schedules the dumpster/compactor to be picked-up at 7 AM on Sunday morning? It woke up the entire block. Unfortunately, our entire floor had been awakened at 6:30 AM by Sheraton security looking to reunite Mr [NAME] with his lost wife. I've got one word for you fools: discretion. Look it up! And while your at it, wise up. 
The room would have been ok if the deadbolt actually locked, the night stand drawer actually opened and the shower actually drained, but hey...if they don't give a crap about waking you at 6:30 AM on a Sunday morning.....why would they worry about the comfort and safety of their rooms? Don't pay full price to stay here. Use Priceline and you can book a night for a hundred bucks. You'll need to save every penny because parking will set you back $51.30 a night. On the plus side, the staff is very friendly and they will let you check in early if they have rooms available. Don't be shy about asking.

title_masked: More like a hostel than a hotel
text_masked:
This hotel was more like a Hostel, the rooms were small and a little shabby but adequate and were cleaned daily. A central kitchen on the 3rd floor means you can expect quite a bit of noise if you happen to be anywhere near there of on any stairwell. 
That said the place is cheap for San Francisco, we paid $85 a night for a double room.
Location is good. The best part for us was "Eric" the guy on the front desk who was really helpful. 
So if you can do without the creature comforts and are on a bit of a budget this place does what is says on the tin.

We stayed two nights at the Palomar. The facility is typical Kimpton offbeat chic with the only drawback the relative smallness of the room. The service and attitude of the staff is what really sets this property apart. Everyone is exceptionally friendly and helpful and are adept at graciousness. The location is very good and near all the attractions and many of the better restaurants. The staff here make this one of the better places we have stayedand an excellent choice for Philadelphia.

Big conference oriented hotel, with a great location if you want to be near the Capitol, union station, and east end of the Mall. Clean rooms, comfortable beds. Appeared to be people using wifi in the lobby, but we never managed to get on in room. Valet parking is available - but be aware that it's $45 a night (though they did say this include in and out if you need it). Quick return of car on check out if you use their text for your car feature. Room set up was a little disappointing - no table or light on 1 side of bed, alarm clock/ihome was missing power cord, and no in-room safe. Location was great for our needs - walked to a concert at Nationals stadium (about 1 mile south) and took a great run on the Mall Saturday morning (about 3 miles round trip to the Washington Monument from the hotel). Breakfast is good, but hard to say the buffet is worth $21 - there's a starbucks around the corner that would probably be a better bet. There is surprisingly little choice in restaurants right near the hotel - so plan to venture more than a few blocks to eat.

The word Suite is a joke and a bad one at best. The room I reserved was so small that the "opened the door and crawled across the bed" cliche applies. Their web site shows suites but their so called suites are 40% more expensive than their cracker barrell rooms. Place was clean but wi fi signal was almost non existent. Never again Wyndham for me.

I rented two rooms during the Maryland primary elections, one for my wife and one for two other people that were from out of state to work the elections. I had gotted an email from choice hotels to get a discounted room upgrade to which I took for my wife and I. Our room had a wirlpool tub. Our first day there I used it and it did not work, so the next day when my work crew showed up i mentioned it to the manager and asked if we could get a room that had one that work. I was told no that I got the room at a discounted rate, and he also refused to get it repaired while we were there. When I complained to choicehotel.com the contacted the hotel to find out what happend and told me that they should have an answer for me in 24 to 48 hours. I called back and they had not heard from him but gave me extra points for my problems

Tabard Inn is a landmark, and it is fun walking through the labyrinth of halls with old and dusty furniture. The restaurant is very popular and usually booked for dinner and brunch. The lunch of pumpkin soup and beet salad was well done. We stayed in Room 54 which is large with a seating area in the front of the building. The bathroom was fun, but needed better lighting.
