The bed was comfortable enough with nice bedding. The building is quaintly creaky and voices carried through the walls. Breakfast that came with the room was pretty good. The lounge is very nice with a real fireplace, but not enough lighting for reading. Some of the staff were not service oriented and minimally friendly. Street parking is pretty much unavailable, unless you are very lucky. Valet parking is an extra $25/night. A clearer fire escape plan would be appreciated since the building is very old. It is feeling a little tired, so the Tabard Inn could use a good cleaning, better lighting, and a bit of updating...all of which would contribute to its charming ambiance, because it is a cool and fun place in the heart of DC.
Great hotel. Very good service. Large rooms. Excellent Amenities. Great location.

3 girls who wanted to stay downtown without spending a fortune! I am not a picky person when it comes to staying at a hotel as long as the rooms are nice. I think this hotel has a long way to go. It doesn't give the greatest impression on the outside. When we walked in the room was nice! We only slept there one night so my review is based on this. As the night progressed it got more and more moist. By morning the carpet felt dewy. And it was really noisy. Right next to Interstate. It is at a great location and has great potential. I just think it needs a little more work done.

Clean enough. Rooms are somewhat dated. I stayed two night 2/15 - 2/16. The noise from he room above was worthy of complaint but the " guy" obviulsy didnt want the confrontation...so I called up to the room. The next day same noise. This time a lady dealt with it and they quietened down. Small pool and jacuzzi. Ok. Nothing special. The little shop they ahve is WAY expensive. There is a 7 Eleven across the road and they too were WAY expensive. I live in Denver and was staying while some work was being done on the apartment. So knowing 7 Eleven prices in town..wow...watch out. They have you cornered. It's an Ok hotel but nothing special. One night stay would be enough. Village Inn close by and their prices seemed ok.

We spent 2 nights (Friday and Saturday) there and had a room overlooking the parking lot below. The parking lot that charges $22 per night... I don't know why people say it includes breakfast. It doesn't and we booked straight through the hotel. Not any fancy online sights. The room is tiny, the bathroom even smaller. The towels had blood stains on them. They knew we were a family and only put 3 towels in the bathroom and one of each soap. You could hear the trains nearby. San Diego is such a beautiful place. Spend your money elsewhere.

This Motel 6 is bad on so many levels. Usually Motel 6's are cheap and still nice places to stay; I have used them in quite a few states in US by now. I booked this Motel 6 in Houston for 12 days, and had already decided to move to another motel the next day. The first impression, as many other reviews have written here, is that the motel is increadibly noisy, being near a large highway. When checkin in, the clerk told me the internet was down and the pool was under reparation... Then going up to 3rd floor, I noticed the walls in the corridors looked like the walls of an underground bunker, not of a hotel! Then the room: Well, the room was probably the only positive thing. It was clean and large, although the floor didn't have carpet but solid "laminate" type covering, which is strange for a hotel, but OK. The bathroom was quite new and very clean. During the night, I could hear the neighbors speaking on the phone (I think); the walls do not seem to be that thick. During all the evening, there were two police in front of the building talking to a non-police person for hours. I have no idea what they were doing, but have police for hours in front of your hotel is never a good sign. One other good point though: The staff was friendly, and totally understood when I cancelled the rest of my stay. I know moved to the 'La Quinta Inns & Suites'. I'm writing this review from the 'La Quinta' hotel room, which b.t.w. has free (and working) wifi, and already I'm so happy to be here now! That being said, I still think most Motel 6's are OK, just not the 'Houston Reliant Park' one.

I really was surprised by the clean and modern, but comfortable!, decor at the Doubletree. My room was on the top floor and had an unusual shape that gave it character. The bed was very comfortable and was very quiet even though I was relatively close to the elevators. My only complaint was that the toilet was positioned that I kept hitting my knees on the door. Otherwise a great stay with very nice staff. Don't pass up the warm cookie at check in!

title_masked: Smells Terrible like a smokey bar room
text_masked: When I checked in to this hotel, the smell of smoke was so overwhelming, I should have turned around and gone home. I had pre paid, unfortuneately. I love marriotts, normally, and this was equal to a motel 6, except for the cost! No coffee offered in the lobby on a Sunday morning, no extra's at all. The view out of our window was apartments, the shabby low rent type. I was extremely disappointed as you can surely tell! Oh, did I mention that I am a smoker and even though, the stink was nauseating. BTW this was a Marriotts Courtyard Hotel, but there was NO courtyard. The residence inn across the lake looks like a courtyard but is actually a Residence Inn. My Bad for sure!

Briefly, the service lacked in courtesy and efficiency. When we needed to get new rooms keys because ours stopping working, the desk clerk was curt, as if we were bothering her. When one of the people in our group could not access his safe in his room, no one could help him until the maintenance man came in....not even the security personell! The access hallway to the pool is a dirty, back stairwell and creepy. The room air conditioners are noisy and ...if you want to open your sliding glass door, you better be iron man!

title_masked: For the room quality we got, we should have just stayed at the Motel 6.
text_masked:
I should have read the reviews for this place before booking it, but I've stayed at a Quality Inn before and they have been decent for the price so was expecting the same standards.
Firstly, we were told the room would have two double beds, they were more like king single beds. Also it was suppose to be a non-smoking room but someone had been smoking in the bathroom previous to our stay. 
The room also had a very unpleasant smell, we had to leave the door open to air the room out. I also used lysol spray and that helped a bit but overnight when we had to close the door, the smell was there again in the morning.
The chairs in the room were stained, the towels that were provided were shabby. Shower head in bathroom had black mould. 
I would not stay here again, I feel for the price we paid $99 plus tax we should have just gone to the motel 6 down the road. At least there you get what you pay for. 
No issues with the staff, just the room.

title_masked: Great for budget travelers, but not very comfortable
text_masked:
I had a quick business trip to NYC for an overnight. As I was on a budget, this was one of the few conveniently located hotels about. I've stayed at the Pod before. I like it because of it's location and cleanliness.
But it isn't that comfortable, given the tiny size of the rooms. The concept is cute. A ship pod. This time, during the heat wave in NYC, my air conditioner conked out around 1:30 am. I was miserable tossing and turning in 90 degree sweltering heat. I knew if I called downstairs they would not have a maintenance man come up in the middle of the night to tinker and fix it. I tried my best, having dealt with faulty systems before. I managed to fix it for about 20 minutes. And then it conked out again. Needless to say I got no sleep and was pretty cranky and tired the next day. 
I guess I am getting older, but having to get up in the middle of the night to go to the bathroom down the hall isn't fun anymore. But that's me, and no fault of the hotel. LOL. At least they are clean, and there is a cool alert system in your room that indicates which loos are taken. 
I will say this is great for backpackers and young couples and families on a budget. Not sure I am going to stay here anymore.
Stayed one night. Very clean room, modern amenities. Very attentive staff. Will definitely return.

Don't like to write bad reviews, but felt I had to...I was told a check in we could get a roll in bed since we brought the kids double beds are kinda small....Find out later (after we chose our room) thats against fire code...OK..I get it....Things happen..Thought with an extra blanket I would hit the floor and momma and the kids would be drama free..till 1am found that the heater was blowing cold air..only 62 degrees in the room..Seriously considered going to the parking garage and sleeping in the suv..the floor is concrete my beanie and jacket wasn't working and the blanket ( too short) only covered me in fetal position and my heat escaped when i rolled over from shoulder to shoulder the only thin sleeping....now back at home in az and all the kids have fevers..but they were sorry and offered us a continental breakfast....save your money..motels are on one floor..you park in front of your room..(not a huge parking garage that you pay a ton of fees and walk a mile to get to..) they are bigger and cleaner..and usually closer to the beach..not to mention half the price and all the service..Troy in az..Have a blessed day..

Stayed for two nights (Saturday and Sunday).
Terrible 1st night. The bar across the street played loud music til well after midnight. To make things worse, you can hear clearly from your bed people talking in the hallway and barking dogs from room next door. Not a good night, especially after a long 20-plus hour flights.
Ice machine didn't dispense ice on the second day (99 degree F day).
Coffee was not refilled by the cleaning service.
I first book the hotel because of the location. But it turns out to be quite a walk to the 16th street mall (downtown area), and even quite far from "Denver Bicycle" stations. If i knew all this, i would spend an extra U$10-20 to stay in, say Hilton Garden Inn. Much much better location, service, room, etc.

title_masked: Terrific and large room, fastest room service ever and overall great statt
text_masked: After reading the mixed review of this property, I was a bit uneasy. But after staying - I'm a fan. I was booked into a Deluxe Room in the newer section and the room was quite nice. Very large room with a very large bathroom. While every room details wasn't what I'd consider 5-star, the overall feel, quality and comforts were - and it was an outstanding stay. Perhaps the most amazing part of my stay was room service - it was lightening fast. I've never experienced such speedy and quality room service. Even on a night when they were swamped and I was told 45-minutes, it was less than 30 and most meals were about 15 or 20 minutes max. The public space was nice and the front-desk staff as well as housekeeping were terrific Love the location and having stayed at a lot of San Francisco hotels, I'd happily return to the Westin St. Francis.

title_masked: The Post hotel is not a good place to rest your head.
text_masked:
This hotel may have asbestos in the rooms and hallways. The owner/manager has "painted" over instead of removing the asbestos.
The elevator may or may not work.

Stayed here over Easter with husband and 2 teenage daughters on the 14th floor. Very clean room and plenty of hot water. Great location as only a short walk to Empire State and about 15-20 mins stroll to Times Square. Got breakfast inc. in room rate which was great not having to find somewhere to eat early in the morning. Plenty of Frosties, fruit, croissants, scrambled egg on toast, etc. All good, and the ladies waiting on the tables were lovely, serving huge glasses of OJ. If you are a light sleeper, take ear plugs because the horn blowing goes on at all times. Also, the florists in the road where the hotel is start to set up early in the morning. Looks beautiful when you wake up and look down at all the flowers. The only grumble was with the air con unit. It's under the window sill and is very noisy when it fires up in the middle of the night. Apart from that, it's all you need ... Clean room, hot water, fresh towels every day and a good location and they don't mind looking after your suitcases for a couple of hours after you've checked out. PS: to the Manager ... the windows on the 14th floor could do with a clean :)

i don't know what's the deal with the front desk attendant ( not sure what his name is but it's the elder guy he talks with an accent ) . but for some reason he is very rude. ok he called my room saying people keep calling my room back to back, so i replied i didn't receive any calls. then he replied tell people to stop calling you we are busy here , and when i tried to respond he kept talking well actually fussing at me as though i was his child then hung up the phone..he was very very very rude and this wasn't his first time speaking to me in this manner. he was unprofessional. and by the way how can i tell someone not to call if i don't know if their calling

We stayed here for one night to visit a family member at John Hopkins. Although the hotel was clean and in close proximity to the ball field, I would not choose this hotel again. I tried to get some
sleep after a long drive only to be awakened by rude patrons from 11:30 until about 4:00am yelling and laughing in the hallways. It appeared that this hotel was used for something other than sleeping. 
The so called valet was parking our car in the small paved area in front of the hotel or on the 
busy street next to 2 bars. I really did not need this extra worry about my car getting damaged.
I would recommend staying in the Harbor East area at the Hilton Garden Inn or the Homewood Suites. Harbor East offered many more nice options for dining and shopping. There is a Whole Foods store right around the corner and many nice shops to browse in.

title_masked: Don't be fool by 5 Million Renovation ads.
text_masked:
Great Location very convenience to subway with attractive big lobby didnt made up for such a small room, black mold between bath room tile and $39 self parking for the 4 stars price. 
Boston is beautiful out door flea market is a short subway ride where you could shop and have a 'BEST' New England clam chowder served in the round bread in the food court.. delicious better than an exclaimed Legal Sea Food. such a beautiful City. nw

This Crowne Plaza is not up to the usual CP standards. Dated decor and furniture in the rooms, and not the type of Crowne Plaza I'm used to. 
Pro's - Parking is reasonable with the self-park and it is connected via an under-road tunnel. 
Cons - Old Decor. Too far to be considered part of the core "Riverwalk" attraction area. It is about a mile from the busy restaraunts and while this could be a plus with a quiet environment, the hotel was noisy the weekend we stayed there.
The biggest problem on this saturday was about half the children in Mexico City were staying here for a soccer tournament. They had little supervision and were running the elevators to every floor and setting off fire alarms all evening on Saturday.
I SHOULD HAVE PAID MORE ATTENTION TO THE NEGATIVE REVIEWS.
